card.name: The word per before a unit
card.fires_on: The word "per" (or "a" or "/m" meaning per) right after a quantity or count noun, where a time or population unit comes next. Seen in rates like "bu. per acre" and "cases per 10,000 women".

modes.label: Rates of yield or frequency
modes.description: "per" follows a measured amount and leads into a unit such as acre, second or page.
modes.example: grow 60 or even 85 bu.<< per>> acre yields when the national average is closer

modes.label: Cases per population
modes.description: "per" follows a count of cases and leads into a population size.

modes.label: Per time period
modes.description: "a" stands for per before day, or a slash form stands for per in a dose unit.
modes.example: two to three hours of water<< a>> day

card.writes: It promotes time-unit words such as day, minute, hour, month and year, so it adds a time unit after "per".
card.plain: It marks the spot where a rate is being written, just before the "per" unit such as per day or per year.
